text:
mara: ran a long seqlen sweep and captured an nsys trace for the 8k case. something odd with KV reads — HBM looks saturated but kernel time doesn't explain it fully
jon: pinged — link to trace?
infra-bot: profile uploaded: https://s3.redwood-internal/profiles/1782233345.nsys :white_check_mark:
mar a: thanks infra-bot (typo) — attaching quick summary below

mara: TL;DR: microbatch=1, seqlen=8192, model=bison-7B-serve, workload=single-stream generation. nsys shows sustained DRAM bandwidth ~700-740 GB/s on node (A100-80GB topo). GPU-util only ~55% and big gaps between cublasGemm and attention kernels.

samir: here are the raw counters I pulled from nsys report:
```
Duration: 2.1s
Total GPU work: 1.15s
Memcpy H2D/D2H: 0.12s
KV fetch kernels (kv_read, kv_assemble): 0.48s
Other kernels (fused_attn, matmul): 0.55s
Estimated HBM BW: 720 GB/s sustained
```

liyu: 720 GB/s seems high but plausible on HBM2. Does the timeline show lots of small scattered loads? That would explain low compute/ high bw usage.

mara: exactly — perfetto/timeline shows a stampede of tiny KV-read kernels interleaved with matmuls. Each KV read is tiny (few KB) but tens of thousands per batch. Microbatch=1 exposes a readstorm.

jon: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? even a small ascii helps.

mara: sure — simplified timeline (nsys slice):
```
[0.00s] cublasGemm (128 ms)
[0.13s] kv_read (3 ms)
[0.14s] kv_assemble (2 ms)
[0.16s] memcpy (1 ms)
[0.17s] fused_attn (95 ms)
[0.28s] kv_read (4 ms)
[0.33s] kv_assemble (3 ms)
[0.36s] gap (10 ms)
[0.46s] cublasGemm (120 ms)
... repeated many times
```

samir: so small kernels + frequent launches — overhead + memory-bound ops. Kernel selection likely falls back to a non-batched KV path because batch boundaries mismatch. Batching heuristic might be detecting small batch sizes and choosing single-request KV kernels.

rachel: I remember we have a microbatch aggregation in routing layer that should coalesce KV operations across concurrent requests, but single-stream generation disables that. Could we enable an intra-request batching policy for long seqlen flows?

mara: good point. I ran an experiment with a naive prefetch: merge KV reads from next 64 tokens into a single larger kernel — dram BW drops to ~420 GB/s and GPU-util jumps to ~78%. End-to-end latency improved 18%.

liyu: did you change kernel selection or just fused the calls on CPU before launching a bigger GPU kernel?

mara: fused on CPU -> launched a single larger kv_read that does a contiguous read + assemble on GPU. So kernel selection used the larger path (vectorized loads + fewer launches).

jon: this suggests two levers: 1) change batching heuristic to prefer aggregated KV ops when seqlen large; 2) implement a fused kv kernel that handles multi-token fetches efficiently.

samir: also check page thrash — perf shows some short spikes in device memory allocation/free around KV eviction windows. Could be our KV page eviction policy causing extra copies.

mara: yes saw nvprof counters that hinted at repeated device->device memcpy around eviction times. When seq grows >6k we hit the threshold and evict older KV pages which triggers D2D copies. Eviction policy + access pattern = thrash.

rachel: options: increase reserved KV pool, LRU tweak to keep hot keys pinned, or prefer streaming mode that writes older KV to slower storage instead of evicting to device. But pinned memory cost might be high for Dedicated customers.

liyu: for immediate fix, can we try: bump microbatching window for long-seq clients, enable fused-kv-prefetch, and disable aggressive eviction for sequences with >4096 tokens? Quick A/B to see perf/regression.

mara: I'll prepare a test branch with a heuristic: if seqlen>=4096 -> coalesce KV reads into windows of 32 tokens and set eviction_threshold += 50%. Running A/B on staging now.

infra-bot: perf artifacts for branch 'kv-prefetch-heuristic' uploaded: https://s3.redwood-internal/profiles/kv-prefetch-1782233345.nsys

jon: nice. keep an eye on p99 latency. coalescing helps throughput but may increase 1st-token latency.

mara: initial numbers: throughput +25%, p50 latency -10%, p99 latency +6% (still within SLO). I'll push results into the rollout doc and tag eng-runtime for review.

samir: long-term, we should add a kernel-selection metric in the console: fraction of KV ops served by 'vectorized' vs 'single' kernels + HBM bandwidth per model. Could automate heuristic tuning.

rachel: agree. also add a regression alert: sudden jump in HBM BW or memcpy fraction -> flag potential KV thrash.

jon: thanks mara — saved us from chasing a phantom compute regression. Looks like bandwidth-bound KV behavior + small-kernel launch overhead. Great detective work. :trophy:
